visibleStrings: Aubade lives on your machine and nowhere else. It reads your folders, sings your lyrics back in time and never asks for an account. Five thousand tracks, indexed before the kettle boils.
SIDE A — THE CASE FOR QUIET
The whole app reads like a morning poem.
An aubade is a poem lovers trade at dawn.
The player by that name takes after it —
Your music stays in your folders. So does Aubade.
No account signs you in. No library leaves home.
One keystroke pulls a song from five thousand.
The day can start with the chorus. It usually does.
THIS PAGE RUNS ALONE: NO TRACKERS, NO BANNER ADS, NO BACKGROUND CALLS.
Your music is a folder, and Aubade reads it in place. Files never leave the machine that bought them — the cloud gets to live in its own story, on someone else's page.
A 30Hz karaoke clock keeps every line in step with the vocal — glowing when it sings, dimming when it rests. Typography that finally keeps time.
FLAC and Opus keep their true names. The dock prints OPUS 44.1 like a press stamp — what you hear is exactly what the file says, and nothing pretends to be richer than that.
Ctrl K opens one command field that reaches the whole library — search, queue, play, jump. Two hands stay where they usually are: on the keys.
One floating island holds transport, lyrics and queue in eighty-two calm pixels. It rises when you reach for it and keeps out of the way when you listen.
The index lives in memory, so thousands of titles stay a keystroke apart. Type three letters — the answer was already waiting for you.
Index numbers, runtimes, and nothing pretending to be a feed.
Blue hour, hold on to the quiet
